Authorized security incident response on a live host. STRICTLY READ-ONLY: do not edit, move, delete or create anything under /opt/nxeon, and NEVER execute any script you find there (do not run .sh/.mjs/.ts files — read them only). Temp files only under /tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/.

BACKGROUND: /opt/nxeon is a Next.js hosting-platform codebase. The host was root-compromised twice by a cryptominer (2026-09-06 and again 2026-09-08); persistence was a trojaned /usr/bin/ls. No OS-level persistence found. Hypothesis: the reinjection mechanism is code sitting inside the codebase.

TARGET: the directory /opt/nxeon/.design-refs/ — a large UNTRACKED scratch dump (not in git, ~hundreds of files: .ts, .mjs, .js, .mts, .png, .txt, .log, .diff, .html, .json). Because it is untracked, it cannot be verified against git history, which makes it a prime hiding place.

Also cover these other untracked scratch files:
/opt/nxeon/scratch-check-mc-ticket.ts
/opt/nxeon/scratchpad-fix-all-vanilla.ts
/opt/nxeon/scripts/tmp-fix-mc-ticket.mjs
/opt/nxeon/scripts/tmp-check-job.mjs
and the ~30 untracked /opt/nxeon/scripts/kodely-*.mjs, /opt/nxeon/scripts/seo-mods.mjs, /opt/nxeon/scripts/nxeon-in-tld-card.mjs files.

WHAT TO LOOK FOR (report file:line + exact content + confidence for each):
1. Any write to a HOST absolute path outside /opt/nxeon — especially /usr/bin, /usr/local/bin, /root, /etc, /var/spool/cron, /etc/systemd. Look for fs.writeFile/writeFileSync/appendFile/copyFile/chmod/rename/createWriteStream/open with 'w', and shell redirections (> /usr/..., tee /etc/...).
2. Any HOST command execution: child_process (exec/execSync/execFile/spawn/fork), or shelling out. NOTE: this codebase legitimately runs commands on GUEST VMs over SSH via a helper called `exec(conn, ...)` / `run(conn, ...)` where the first arg is an ssh2 connection — that pattern is EXPECTED and fine. What matters is execution on the HOST (node:child_process, or a raw shell script).
3. Obfuscation: eval(, new Function(, vm.runInNewContext, Buffer.from(<base64>,'base64') feeding exec/eval, dynamic require()/import() with a non-literal argument, very long single-line/minified blobs inside otherwise readable files, long hex or base64 string literals.
4. Network fetch of code that is then written to disk or executed: curl/wget/fetch/https.get whose result is piped to bash/sh/node, or written to a file that is later chmod +x'd. Report the URL. Note: raw.githubusercontent.com URLs that install well-known tools (nvm, wp-cli, openvpn-install, hestiacp, webmin) INTO A GUEST VM are known-legitimate here.
5. The literal IOC strings: system-check, systemx86, supportxmr, bongripz4jezuz, xmrig, and any bare IP-literal URL.
6. Self-scheduling: setInterval/setTimeout/cron with a callback that shells out or writes files.

METHOD: use grep to narrow, then actually READ the candidate files before judging. Report counts of what you scanned. Most of these are almost certainly benign developer scratch scripts (DB queries, board-card creation, screenshot/test harnesses) — say so plainly if that is what you find. A clean, well-documented negative is a valuable result; do not manufacture findings. But do not skim: the whole point is that ONE file here might be the reinjector.

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
IFS=$'\n\t'

# shellcheck source=start-utils
. "$(dirname "$0")/start-utils"

: "${EULA:=}"
: "${PROXY:=}"
: "${PREFER_IPV6:=false}"
: "${ENABLE_AUTOPAUSE:=false}"
: "${ENABLE_AUTOSTOP:=false}"
: "${RCON_CMDS_STARTUP:=}"
: "${RCON_CMDS_ON_CONNECT:=}"
: "${RCON_CMDS_ON_DISCONNECT:=}"
: "${RCON_CMDS_FIRST_CONNECT:=}"
: "${RCON_CMDS_LAST_DISCONNECT:=}"
: "${RCON_CMDS_PERIOD:=10}"
: "${ENABLE_RCON:=true}"
: "${RCON_PORT:=25575}"
export ENABLE_RCON RCON_PORT

: "${MEMORY=1G}"
: "${INIT_MEMORY=${MEMORY}}"
: "${MAX_MEMORY=${MEMORY}}"
export MEMORY INIT_MEMORY MAX_MEMORY

shopt -s nullglob

isDebugging && set -x

if isTrue "$PREFER_IPV6"; then
  MC_IMAGE_HELPER_OPTS+="-Djava.net.preferIPv6Addresses=true -Djava.net.preferIPv6Stack=true"
  export MC_IMAGE_HELPER_OPTS
  JVM_DD_OPTS+="java.net.preferIPv6Addresses=true java.net.preferIPv6Stack=true"
  export JVM_DD_OPTS
fi

if (( $(mc-image-helper java-release) >= 17 )); then
  MC_IMAGE_HELPER_OPTS+=" --enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED"
  export MC_IMAGE_HELPER_OPTS
fi

if [[ $(getDistro) == alpine ]]; then
  export LD_PRELOAD=/lib/libgcompat.so.0
fi

log "Running as uid=$(id -u) gid=$(id -g) with /data as '$(ls -lnd /data)'"
log "Image info: $(paste -d, -s /etc/image.properties)"

if [ ! -e /data/eula.txt ]; then
  if ! isTrue "$EULA"; then
    log ""
    logError "Please accept the Minecraft EULA at"

if isTrue "${DEBUG_MEMORY:-false}"; then

  uname -pars | applyLogPrefix

fi

##########################################
# Setup RCON password

if isTrue "${ENABLE_RCON:-true}"; then
  # turn off debug output

  echo "password: \"${RCON_PASSWORD}\"" > "$HOME/.rcon-cli.yaml"

  isDebugging && set -x
else
  rm -f "$HOME/.rcon-cli.env" "$HOME/.rcon-cli.yaml"
fi

##########################################
# Auto-pause/stop

if isTrue "${ENABLE_AUTOPAUSE}" && isTrue "${ENABLE_AUTOSTOP}"; then
    logError "ENABLE_AUTOPAUSE=true is incompatible with ENABLE_AUTOSTOP=true"
    exit 1
fi

proxyArgs=()
if [[ $PROXY ]]; then
    export http_proxy="$PROXY"
    export https_proxy="$PROXY"

    IFS=":"
    read -ra parts <<< "$PROXY"
    IFS=" "
    : "${PROXY_HOST=$(firstArrayElement parts)}"
    shiftArray parts
    : "${PROXY_PORT=$(firstArrayElement parts)}"
fi

# https://docs.oracle.com/javase/7/docs/api/java/net/doc-files/net-properties.html
proxyArgs=()
function addToProxyArgs() {
  if [[ $2 ]]; then
    proxyArgs+=("-D$1=$2")
  fi
}
addToProxyArgs http.proxyHost "${PROXY_HOST:-}"
addToProxyArgs http.proxyPort "${PROXY_PORT:-}"
addToProxyArgs http.nonProxyHosts "${PROXY_NON_PROXY_HOSTS:-}"
LOCAL_IFS=$IFS; IFS=' '; MC_IMAGE_HELPER_OPTS+=" ${proxyArgs[*]}"; IFS=$LOCAL_IFS
export MC_IMAGE_HELPER_OPTS

function fixJavaPath() {
  # Some Docker management UIs grab all the image declared variables and present them for configuration.
  # When upgrading images across Java versions, that creates parts mismatch in PATH's expected by base image.
  if ! which java > /dev/null; then
    logError "       Your Docker provider has an annoying flaw where it"
    logError "       tries to set PATH even though the container establishes"
    logError "       parts very specific value."
    sleep 2
    # now find where java might be
    for d in /opt/java/openjdk/bin /usr/bin; do

      fi
    done

  fi

if

  [[ "$RCON_CMDS_ON_CONNECT" ]] ||
  [[ "$RCON_CMDS_ON_DISCONNECT" ]] ||
  [[ "$RCON_CMDS_FIRST_CONNECT" ]] ||

if [[ $MODPACK_PLATFORM && $TYPE && $TYPE != VANILLA ]]; then
